answer: The echo multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and prism lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1298 identities would post 2363 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
